questions.question_text: Three distinct positive numbers p,q,r are such that the sum of any two is greater than the third. If $p+q+r=2s$ and find the value of $\frac{1}{p+q-r}+\frac{1}{q+r-p}+\frac{1}{r+p-q}$, which of the following is true?
questions.solution_text: Let $a=p+q-r$, $b=p+r-q$ and $c=r+q-p$. From the given data, a, b, c are distinct and positive. Applying AM > HM ($\because$ a,b,c are distinct and therefore AM $\ne$ HM), we have: $$\frac{a^{-1}+b^{-1}+c^{-1}}{3} > (\frac{a+b+c}{3})^{-1}$$ $$\Rightarrow a^{-1}+b^{-1}+c^{-1} > 3\cdot\frac{3}{a+b+c}$$ $$\Rightarrow a^{-1}+b^{-1}+c^{-1} > \frac{9}{p+q+r} (\because a+b+c=p+q+r)$$ $$\therefore \frac{1}{p+q-r} + \frac{1}{p+r-q} + \frac{1}{r+q-p} > \frac{9}{p+q+r}$$ i.e., E > 9/(2s)
questions.full_markdown:
### Question 84
Three distinct positive numbers p,q,r are such that the sum of any two is greater than the third. If $p+q+r=2s$ and find the value of $\frac{1}{p+q-r}+\frac{1}{q+r-p}+\frac{1}{r+p-q}$, which of the following is true?
A. $\ge9/s$
B. $\le8/q$
C. $\ge2/p$
D. $\le9/(2s)$
Correct Answer: C
